questions.prompt: Why does least squares add up the squared gaps instead of the plain gaps?
options: Squared gaps are faster to compute than plain gaps
Plain gaps above and below the line would cancel, so a bad line could score 0
Squaring turns the slope into a correlation between -1 and 1
Squaring makes the line pass through the point (0, 0)
questions.explanation: A gap of +1 and a gap of -1 add to 0, even though the line missed both dots. Squared, they add to 2, so every miss counts.

questions.prompt: The covariance of x and y is 3.0 and the variance of x is 1.5. What is the slope of the fitted line?
questions.explanation: The slope is the covariance divided by the variance of x: 3.0 / 1.5 = 2.0. So y goes up by 2.0, on average, when x goes up by 1.

questions.prompt: The fitted line is y = 1.3 + 0.9 × x. A dot sits at x = 2, y = 3. What is its residual?
questions.explanation: The line forecasts 1.3 + 0.9 × 2 = 3.1. The residual is the actual y minus the forecast: 3 - 3.1 = -0.1, so the dot sits a little below the line.
